record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How can model-agnostic meta-learning and learning-to-learn methods be adapted to federated learning, including realistic benchmarks, theoretical guarantees, personalized-performance metrics, explanations for why globally optimized models may personalize poorly, treatment of concept drift, and possible non-parameter-transfer algorithms?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the federated learning setting in which a central server coordinates training across a population of clients $\{1,2,\dots,N\}$, where each client $i$ holds a local data distribution $\mathcal{D}_i$ over an input-output space $\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$ and the distributions $\mathcal{D}_i$ may be statistically heterogeneous (non-IID) and may drift over time. A model is parameterized by $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^d$, with a loss $\ell(\theta;x,y)$ and per-client risk $F_i(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal{D}_i}[\ell(\theta;x,y)]$.

In the model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) / learning-to-learn formulation of personalization, the server seeks an initialization $\theta^\star$ such that, after a small number $k\geq 1$ of local adaptation steps $U_i^k(\theta)$ (e.g., gradient steps on $F_i$), the personalized parameters $\theta_i:=U_i^k(\theta^\star)$ achieve low local risk. A natural objective is
$$\min_{\theta\in\mathbb{R}^d}\ \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N F_i\bigl(U_i^k(\theta)\bigr).$$
More generally, "non-parameter-transfer" personalization replaces $U_i^k$ by transfer mechanisms that do not consist solely of fine-tuning a shared parameter vector (e.g., hypernetworks, modular components, prototype/embedding transfer, or data-dependent personalization maps).

Develop a theory and methodology for federated meta-learning addressing all of the following:

(a) Construct realistic benchmark task distributions and evaluation protocols for federated meta-learning that reflect cross-device and cross-silo deployments, including non-IID clients, system heterogeneity, partial participation, communication constraints, and temporal concept drift in $\{\mathcal{D}_i\}_{i,t}$.

(b) Establish theoretical guarantees (convergence rates, sample/communication complexity, and generalization bounds to held-out and to newly-arriving clients) for federated MAML-type algorithms under realistic assumptions on heterogeneity, stochastic gradients, partial participation, and Hessian access in the inner update.

(c) Define and analyze rigorous personalized-performance metrics that measure post-adaptation accuracy across the client population (including tail/worst-client behavior, fairness across clients, and few-shot adaptation on new clients), and prove their relation to the global meta-objective above.

(d) Provide a mathematical characterization explaining when and why a globally optimal model $\theta_G^\star\in\arg\min_\theta \frac{1}{N}\sum_i F_i(\theta)$ personalizes poorly, i.e., quantify the gap
$$\Delta\;=\;\frac{1}{N}\sum_i F_i(\theta_G^\star)\;-\;\frac{1}{N}\sum_i F_i\bigl(U_i^k(\theta^\star)\bigr)$$
in terms of geometric or statistical properties of $\{F_i\}$ (curvature, task similarity, conditioning).

(e) Extend the framework to handle concept drift, where $\mathcal{D}_i$ is replaced by a time-varying $\mathcal{D}_{i,t}$, with provable tracking/adaptation guarantees.

(f) Design and analyze non-parameter-transfer federated meta-learning algorithms that go beyond a shared initialization, with formal guarantees comparable to (b)–(d).

Determine to what extent each of (a)–(f) admits a complete solution.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists: Fallah–Mokhtari–Ozdaglar (NeurIPS 2020) established convergence and first-order-optimality guarantees for Per-FedAvg, a MAML-based personalized federated learning algorithm, and Jiang et al. (2019) gave empirical MAML-based personalization results. Subsequent work (2023–2025) has produced clustered/co-meta-learning variants, hypernetwork-based personalization (pFedHN/pFedLA), and reinforcement-learning-style personalization addressing heterogeneity. However, comprehensive realistic benchmarks, tight theoretical guarantees under partial participation and concept drift, fairness-aware personalization metrics with provable links to the meta-objective, and provably effective non-parameter-transfer algorithms remain only partially addressed, so the overall program is still open in significant parts.

status_evidence.title: Personalized Federated Learning with Theoretical Guarantees: A Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes convergence properties of Per-FedAvg and characterizes complexity for first-order optimality in nonconvex settings.
status_evidence.claim: Partial theoretical guarantees exist for federated MAML.

status_evidence.title: Improving Federated Learning Personalization via Model Agnostic Meta Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Connects FedAvg with MAML and shows empirical personalization improvements.
status_evidence.claim: Early empirical work connecting MAML and federated personalization.

status_evidence.title: Personalized Federated Learning: A Clustered Distributed Co-Meta-Learning approach
status_evidence.claim: Continuing research on heterogeneity-aware federated meta-learning.

status_evidence.title: An efficient personalized federated learning approach in heterogeneous environments
status_evidence.snippet: Notes existing personalized FL methods do not adequately address data and system heterogeneity.
status_evidence.claim: Realistic benchmark and heterogeneity challenges remain open.
